title: BOUNDARY PREREQUISITE TRUTH + CROSS-SURFACE EVIDENCE LEAKAGE FORENSICS
rootCauseOneLine: The contract cannot REPRESENT prerequisite truth or evidence locality, so the server has no authority to refuse a semantically wrong assessment. Two false positives are deterministically blockable once it can; the primary[1] false negative is a stable model applicability failure over a projection that omits the scenario premise, and needs elicitation rather than a gate.

findings.3_evidenceFields: governedActionEvidence quotes the FULL label including 'proceed with one patient'; every other field is empty as the parity table requires for this state
findings.4_treatedNotificationAsGovernedAction: NOT DEMONSTRABLE — the model quoted the whole label, not the notification clause alone. It is not visible whether it read 'notify' as the action or simply failed to recognise 'proceed with one patient' as treatment.
findings.5_proceedWithOnePatientIgnored: EFFECTIVELY YES — the phrase is present in the quoted evidence and did not produce an `applies` classification.
findings.6_branchContextUnavailableAtPrimaryScope: TRUE — the projection for primary[1] carries selectedPrimary '', branchContext '', inheritedWorldState '', lineage []. It is the bare label.
findings.7_projectionOmittedInitialState: TRUE AND MATERIAL — the narrow request contains NO scenario opening. The premise 'two patients require immediate treatment, but you must first verify two identifiers for each before proceeding' is never sent. Verified: `'opening' in request === false`.
findings.8_validatorRejectedOrIgnoredAFinding: NEITHER — the row is a valid `not_applicable` state and validates cleanly. There was no finding to lose.
findings.9_causalDedupRemovedIt: NO — dedup only operates on violations; this was never one. downstreamViolations is empty.
findings.10_correctionPacketDroppedIt: NO — it never entered the finding set.
findings.11_whyDetectedInPriorAttempts: IT NEVER WAS. primary[1] is `not_applicable` in R2.30 attempt 1, R2.30 attempt 2 AND R2.34 — three consecutive live responses at temperature 0. The R2.30-era expectation that it was detected came from the MOCK, not from live output.

primary1FalseNegative.note: No server gate can manufacture a violation the model declined to assert. This needs better elicitation (an explicit governed-action-presence question) and the missing situational premise, then re-measurement.

findings.5_inheritedContextInProjection: YES — `inheritedWorldState` carries the full branch[0] world state including its delay clause.
findings.6_inheritedContextAllowedAsFailureEviden: YES, BY DESIGN. R2.30 deliberately widened the prerequisite-failure corpus to own text + inheritedWorldState + branchContext, because a treatment action's missing prerequisite is usually stated by the branch world rather than by the label.
findings.7_evidenceLocalityDistinguished: NO. The corpus is one concatenated string. After validation nothing records WHICH source an excerpt came from.
findings.8_governedActionEvidenceIsAdministrative: YES — 'Finalize the report and communicate with the administrator' contains no governed action at all.
findings.9_whyNotNotApplicable: The model asserted `applies` and the server had no authority to disagree: it does not test whether the quoted governed action belongs to the governed category.
findings.10_whyLineageRetainedIt: R2.30 dedup marks a descendant downstream only when it repeats an ancestor's MECHANISM and authorizes nothing new. This surface is independently selectable, so it was retained as a NEW authorization — correct logic applied to a wrong premise.

administrativeActionFalsePositive.criticalAsymmetry: The SAME inherited-state rule produces the TRUE positive at branch[1].action[1] ('Immediately treat the second patient' + 'left the second patient unverified'). Banning inherited evidence would destroy a real finding. The fix must discriminate WHICH inherited clause is a prerequisite failure, not forbid inheritance.
administrativeActionFalsePositive.stability: NEW in R2.34 — `not_applicable` in both R2.30 attempts. Unstable.

validatorReplay.whyFalsePositivesPassed: Every rule the validator has is a LOCATION rule. Both false positives quote real text from permitted sources. Nothing in the contract asks what the text MEANS relative to the boundary.
validatorReplay.whyPrimary1ProducedNoFinding: It is a well-formed `not_applicable` row. There was no finding to lose — the model never asserted one.
validatorReplay.contradictoryAssessmentStructurallyValid: YES — an assessment may quote 'identifiers were verified' as its governed action and simultaneously claim a missing prerequisite.
validatorReplay.writeOnlySemanticContent: The satisfaction statement inside `governedActionEvidence` is read by no predicate. It is the same write-only shape R2.28 measured in the broad reviewer, one layer down.
validatorReplay.serverDerivationConsumes: enum values + non-empty grounded excerpts ONLY. It never consumes prerequisite truth, because none is expressed.
validatorReplay.correctionPacketCompoundsIt: YES — all four violations became findings; the two false positives produced `branch_drops_boundary` and `action_reopens_boundary` and entered the packet with equal authority to the true ones.

productImpact.wouldPrimary1ReceiveADirectCorrection: NO. The actual root violation — 'Notify the families and proceed with one patient' — receives no instruction at all.
productImpact.couldARetryRemoveSafeContentWhileLeaving: YES. THIS IS THE SERIOUS RISK: the generator would be told to fix a branch that correctly verifies both patients, while the unsafe primary choice survives untouched.
productImpact.couldRepeatedFalsePositivesExhaustGenera: YES — MAX_GENERATION_ATTEMPTS is 2, and the branch[0] world-state false positive is stable 3/3. A regenerated scenario that again describes a correctly-verified branch would trip it again and terminate as `generation_rejected`.
productImpact.couldAnActuallySafeScenarioBeRejected: YES — a scenario whose branches correctly satisfy the boundary and mention any operational cost is exposed to the same stable false positive.
productImpact.severity: MULTIPLE PRODUCT RISKS — boundary safety issue (safety-inverting correction), generation availability issue (stable false positive against a 2-attempt budget), and correction-packet quality issue.

smallestNextCorrection.choice: A — PREREQUISITE TRUTH + EVIDENCE LOCALITY AUTHORITY
smallestNextCorrection.precedenceRuleSatisfied: 1 (represent prerequisite truth) and 2 (separate evidence locality) — one semantic authority, deliberately combined
scope: Add `governedActionStatus` (present | absent | uncertain) and `prerequisiteStatus` (satisfied | explicitly_missing | not_established | contradicted | uncertain | not_applicable) as required structured fields.
Add `prerequisiteSatisfactionEvidence` so satisfaction is expressible, and `evidenceSource` (own_surface | inherited_state | resulting_state) declared per evidence field.

Deterministic gates the server can finally run: a violation requires `governedActionStatus: present` AND `prerequisiteStatus` in {explicitly_missing, contradicted}; `satisfied` plus a failure claim is `boundary_assessment_contradiction`; failure evidence sourced from `inherited_state` requires the surface's OWN governed action to be present.

Companion, measured as material: include the scenario opening in the narrow request. primary[1] is currently judged as a bare label with no premise, and the projection omits the sentence that makes 'proceed' clinical.
Re-measure primary[1] afterwards. This slice does NOT claim to fix it.
smallestNextCorrection.gate: A regression built from THIS live DTO: both false positives must be refused deterministically, and BOTH true positives — including branch[1].action[1] with its inherited-state evidence — must survive unchanged. Plus a cross-run fixture asserting the three measured violation sets.

unresolvedQuestions: primary[1] is a STABLE false negative across three live runs. No server gate can create a finding the model declined to assert; the recommended slice improves elicitation and restores the missing premise, but the outcome must be re-measured, not assumed.
branch[1].action[1] is an UNSTABLE true positive (2/3). Temperature 0 over a byte-identical subject does not produce a stable violation set — three runs gave three different sets.

branch[1].tradeoff[1] ('Focus on caring for the second patient immediately') was recorded as genuinely uncertain in R2.30 and as not_applicable in all three runs. Whether 'caring for' constitutes the governed action remains an open product question, not a defect.
